title: Ammonite Hatchlings
text: Ammonites hatched from small eggs. Their hatchlings were only about one millimeter across, with a tiny shell.
nxt: Nobody has counted ammonite eggs, but because the babies were so small, scientists think that females laid very many of them.

title: Drifting Plankton
text: The hatchlings were far too small to swim against ocean currents, and the evidence suggests that they drifted near the surface as plankton.
nxt: In normal times, this paid off. Warm water and plenty of phytoplankton let the larvae grow quickly.

title: A Hidden Weakness
text: But there was a hidden weakness. The next generation depended on a steady supply of tiny food floating in the sunlight.
nxt: If that supply failed, a whole generation could starve.

title: Nautilus Eggs
text: The nautilus took the opposite approach. A female lays only a small number of large eggs, each about three centimeters long.
nxt: Inside each egg is a rich supply of yolk, so the embryo carries its own food.

title: The Asteroid
text: Then the asteroid struck, sixty-six million years ago.
nxt: Dust and soot blocked much of the sunlight, and phytoplankton, the base of the ocean food web, suffered a mass die-off.
